verdict.rationale: Obsidian's mobile page claims parity with desktop ('brings the power of our desktop app to your mobile devices') and lists tabs, Command Palette and plugins, and the docs describe a customizable mobile editing toolbar. That is a direct first-party claim of a full-featured app rather than a companion. However, search and linking are documented only in general, not as mobile features. A community report also says the Android app delays saving to storage, which can break git sync and has lost note lines, a real caveat for mobile capture. missing for 10: explicit iOS and Android platform documentation, evidence that search and linking work on mobile, independent hands-on confirmation of mobile feature parity, reliable Android saving.

support.subject: As a power-user, full-featured iOS and Android apps give me my whole knowledge base — capture, search, and linking — not a stripped-down companion

citations.quote: Obsidian Mobile brings the power of our desktop app to your mobile devices.
Mobile toolbar is a customization toolbar for editing notes. When editing a note, you will notice a row of icons at the bottom of the app.
